companies.heading: Check holding and risk limits
companies.body: Reports mention profit reductions around news or weekend holding, and disputed closures involving risk assessments or unclear reasons.
companies.attention: Check holding rules by account type and individual risk limits.

companies.heading: Check the review before payout
companies.body: Reports dispute refusals or closures attributed to concentrated risk, EA disclosures and KYC.
companies.attention: Check permitted strategies separately from disclosures required for review.

companies.heading: Watch device, IP and additional rules
companies.body: Reports mention closures attributed to shared devices or copy trading and refusals disputed over when margin rules applied.
companies.attention: Check device, VPS and IP requirements and which rules applied at purchase.

companies.heading: Check closure conditions as well as payouts
companies.body: Account closures outnumber refusals in the included reports. CID, copy-trading judgments and DD calculations are disputed. News-profit cancellation reports include both acknowledged mistakes and disputes. A newly added post disputes an account closure attributed to a CID match. The author denies sharing a device; the logs and whether a violation occurred have not been independently verified.
companies.attention: Check device identification, DD calculations and treatment of news-trading profits.

companies.heading: An account-closure decision is disputed
companies.body: No refusal or reduction reports are included. One report disputes closure while profitable. Being profitable alone does not establish whether a DD breach occurred.
companies.attention: Compare balance, equity and the DD threshold at closure.

companies.heading: Check how news and holding rules are applied
companies.body: Reports dispute the 1% risk limit and CID judgments. Another author acknowledges a refusal caused by their weekend-holding mistake.
companies.attention: Check the account type, including Swing, holding restrictions and additional risk limits.
companies.review_context: An included review alleges that trades 6 and 25 minutes after a scheduled event were treated as news-rule violations because a speech was still in progress. The post alone does not establish whether the decision was justified.

companies.heading: Check KYC before requesting payout
companies.body: One report says KYC was rejected at payout request and only a participation-fee refund was offered.
companies.attention: Check KYC requirements and timing. One report cannot establish a general trend.

companies.heading: Reports of KYC and device-rule disagreements
companies.body: The two included refusals involve a disputed CID judgment and a claim that KYC contradicted an earlier assurance that it was unnecessary.
companies.attention: Check account-specific KYC and device/network restrictions.

companies.heading: Check trading conditions and support responsiveness
companies.body: One post says a payout of only 30% was proposed because of a dynamic IP. Whether all three reductions share this reason has not been established.
companies.attention: Check normal network switching, tethering and reduction conditions.
companies.review_context: Included reviews also describe unanswered support requests and difficulty resetting an account. Slow replies alone do not establish payout refusal or financial distress.

companies.heading: Read payout-review conditions closely
companies.body: Reports dispute refusals involving copying or coordinated trading, the effective date of VPS rules, margin use and minimum holding time. Added posts report a payout refusal and dispute an account closure based on daily drawdown. Repeated posts about the same drawdown incident count as one report; the correctness of the breach decision remains unverified.
companies.attention: Check purchase-date-specific VPS rules, holding time, risk calculations and payout reviews.

companies.heading: Check how excessive risk is defined
companies.body: One report alleges payout refusal and a reset to evaluation after trading was classified as gambling or one-directional trading.
companies.attention: Check specific prohibited-strategy criteria and warning/reset procedures.

companies.heading: Risk reviews can also affect continued use
companies.body: Reports say rules or supporting evidence were insufficiently explained when trades were judged to involve high lots, excessive risk or abusive trading.
companies.attention: Check lot/risk limits, warnings and the scope of profit reductions.
companies.review_context: An included review also alleges account termination after ten payouts and a conflict between earlier assurances and a later risk decision. The trader denies a breach; the complete trading record has not been independently verified.

companies.heading: Check order execution around economic releases
companies.body: The 2 included firsthand reports contain no refusal, account closure, re-entry ban or profit reduction. This does not mean ordinary reviews contain no complaints.
companies.attention: This does not guarantee an absence of problems. The small sample needs additional information before drawing trends.
companies.review_context: One included review describes orders sometimes taking about a minute during sharp moves around economic releases. This is an individual past experience, not a finding about all current orders.

companies.heading: Check when profits can be cancelled
companies.body: Reports include an acknowledged breach leading to profit cancellation and disputes over payouts after scaling, device IDs and inactivity judgments.
companies.attention: Check whether a breach cancels only profit or also closes the account.

companies.heading: Prior advice and review outcomes may differ
companies.body: One report says previously approved lot sizes were later judged excessive risk, resulting in partial payment and account closure.
companies.attention: Keep support responses and compare them with the applicable terms. The sample is three reports.

companies.heading: Payout and continued access are separate
companies.body: No refusal or reduction reports are included. Authors dispute closures based on past trading or overall assessments and changing explanations. Some describe access ending while profit withdrawal remained permitted.
companies.attention: Distinguish payout eligibility from continued access. Check how past activity and policy changes are applied.

companies.heading: Reasons for refusal or closure are disputed
companies.body: Reports dispute CID, IP or coordinated-trading judgments, or say refusal reasons could not be established. An added post also disputes an account closure based on daily drawdown. Whether the author’s profit-and-loss calculation matches the firm’s assessment remains unverified.
companies.attention: Check trading/device records and the procedure for explaining specific breaches.

companies.heading: Check payout waiting times and trading costs
companies.body: The 4 included firsthand reports contain no refusal, account closure, re-entry ban or profit reduction. This does not mean ordinary reviews contain no complaints.
companies.attention: This does not guarantee an absence of problems. The small sample needs additional information before drawing trends.
companies.review_context: Included reviews describe dissatisfaction with payout waiting times and trading fees. Complaints about waiting do not establish payout refusal.

companies.heading: No refusal, closure or reduction in included reports
companies.body: The 8 included firsthand reports contain no refusal, account closure, re-entry ban or profit reduction. This does not mean ordinary reviews contain no complaints.
companies.attention: This does not guarantee an absence of problems. The small sample needs additional information before drawing trends.

feature.heading: Smart contracts automate payout processing
feature.body: Official materials describe automated eligibility checks and transfers when the required conditions are met.
feature.conditions: Positions must be closed and the request signed; profit and rule requirements apply. Regional or sanctions restrictions and violation reviews may hold processing.
feature.timing: Processing time has not been independently measured from these materials, so instant payout is not asserted.

companies.heading: Check post-challenge paperwork and waiting times
companies.body: The 10 included firsthand reports contain no refusal, account closure, re-entry ban or profit reduction. This does not mean ordinary reviews contain no complaints.
companies.attention: This does not guarantee an absence of problems. The small sample needs additional information before drawing trends.
companies.review_context: Included reviews describe a five-business-day wait for a funded account and contacting support when contract instructions could not be completed on screen. These are distinct from payout refusal.

companies.heading: Check payout conditions and account issuance steps
companies.body: The 37 included firsthand reports contain no refusal, account closure, re-entry ban or profit reduction. This does not mean ordinary reviews contain no complaints.
companies.attention: This does not guarantee an absence of problems; cases outside the collection scope may exist.

feature.heading: Smart contracts automate payout processing
feature.body: Official materials describe automated eligibility checks and transfers when the required conditions are met.
feature.conditions: Conditions include A/B book status, reward eligibility and daily caps. The terms allow suitability checks, corrections, applications and suspensions.
feature.timing: Processing time has not been independently measured from these materials, so instant payout is not asserted.

companies.review_context: An included review says a funded account had not yet been issued. Waiting for account issuance is distinct from payout refusal.

companies.heading: Check additional conditions before payout
companies.body: Both refusal and delay reports are present. Posts discuss waiting periods before trading again after excess risk and changes in explanations of payout requirements.
companies.attention: Check cooldowns, additional-profit requirements and payment-provider processing separately.

companies.heading: A loss assessment is disputed
companies.body: One author distinguishes earlier self-attributed disqualifications from a current loss assessment and closure they consider unfair.
companies.attention: Compare the disputed trade with the threshold; previous failures alone do not refute the present claim.

companies.heading: Review may continue after profits are booked
companies.body: Reports dispute profits being cancelled in a later review after the same trading period passed an earlier review; other reports attribute cancellation to risk management. An added retrospective post disputes a refusal following a first payout request. The specific rule, incident date and firm’s explanation are unconfirmed; this is not a verified finding of an improper refusal.
companies.attention: Check review periods, cancellation calculations and how earlier decisions are treated.

companies.heading: Check where scalping crosses the line
companies.body: Reports dispute refusals based on scalping or tick scalping. Authors say trades held over ten minutes were included or specific criteria were not provided.
companies.attention: Check criteria including profit distance and stop losses, not holding time alone. Do not generalize from four reports.

companies.heading: Check profit cancellation and closure rules
companies.body: Reports include both acknowledged high-lot breaches and disputes over DD calculations, prohibited strategies or unexplained closures.
companies.attention: Distinguish acknowledged breaches from disputes over calculations or discretionary judgments.

companies.heading: Check payout timing and execution conditions
companies.body: The 21 included firsthand reports contain no refusal, account closure, re-entry ban or profit reduction. This does not mean ordinary reviews contain no complaints.
companies.attention: This does not guarantee an absence of problems; cases outside the collection scope may exist.
companies.review_context: Included reviews ask for faster payout processing and describe execution concerns. These are not treated as confirmed refusal or reduction cases.

companies.heading: Access may end because of trading style
companies.body: One report says continued participation in the simulated program was refused because the trading profile was considered more suitable for live capital. This is separate from payout refusal.
companies.attention: Performance and continued access are separate. Check final payments and any proposed transition.

companies.heading: Check profit caps and consistency rules
companies.body: Some authors acknowledge consistency or daily-profit-cap breaches that led to reductions or refusals. These cannot all be described as unexplained refusals.
companies.attention: Check profit caps and consistency calculations before applying. Separate reductions from judgments of unfairness.
The firsthand-report sample is too small to establish a trend. This is not a guarantee that problems cannot occur.

copy_review.scope: 31 company summaries checked against current adopted report counts, preserved original-text reviews and selected ordinary-review originals; not a new full-corpus review.
